analysis.title: It Ain't What Ya Know That Gets You in Trouble
key_insights: 30yr Treasury yields spiked +8bps on the hot CPI print but were up less than 2bps later in the session. BTIG calls this a 'news failure' and says it confirms yields have seen a 'tactical' top.
BTIG says the best tell for an inflection point in a trend is a news failure: when the expected reaction to news does not happen, take notice.
Consensus holds that lower yields are bullish for stocks. BTIG says the pain trade continues to be rates down, Nasdaq down.
Semis have already fallen with rates. If Mag7 also falls with rates, BTIG says that would add conviction to its 'Red October' call.
Volume and volatility are at an inflection: SPY volume ~15% above average, QQQ ~25% above average, SPX near a -1% day, and ~79% of NYSE volume in declining stocks.

Before today, volume was at a two-decade low, Mag7 was the 'Last Man Standing', there had been no -1% SPX down day (longest streak since 2020), and no 80% NYSE downside volume day in nearly a year (longest streak on record back to 1996).
SOX index is down 6 days in a row and SOXX ETF is down 7 days in a row. BTIG says odds favor a bounce soon and that today lines up with a bottom under the 2000 analogy.
BTIG says the next semis bounce is likely one to lean into on the sell side before a more drawn out decline.

sector_views.rationale: SOX down 6 straight days and SOXX down 7. A near-term bounce is likely, but BTIG would sell into it ahead of a longer decline, following the 2000 analogy.
BTIG expects a Nasdaq decline alongside falling rates. Mag7 falling with rates would add conviction to its 'Red October' call.

Mag7 falling with rates would confirm the 'Red October' call.
A semis bounce may be short-lived before a more drawn out decline.

~79% of NYSE volume is in declining stocks, close to an 80% downside volume day. None has occurred in nearly a year, the longest streak on record back to 1996.
